messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I ran a set of continuous-batching experiments focused on 'max tokens-per-batch' + 'max batch size' tuning across our common GPU types (T4, A10, L4, A100, H100). Observed some non-linear cost/latency tradeoffs, and a surprising regression after the kernel-selector change.

Maria: Nice. Can you share the test harness and the main knobs you varied? Also which model/config (seq len, kv behavior)?

Alex: Test harness: our perf-runner (docker image: redwood/perf-runner:canary). Workload: mix of chat-turns with mean request_seq=64, p95=256, and rand prefix reuse to exercise KV cache. Model: open-llama-ish 13B quantized path (int8 fallback on some GPUs). Knobs: max_batch_size {1..64}, max_tokens_per_batch {512,1024,2048,4096,8192}, queue policy (FIFO, priority-by-length, token-aware), and token-budget target (aggressive=90% device fill vs conservative=60%). Kernel selector used: cpu->cudnn/autotune variants + our new fused-attn kernels.

Sam: Which metrics did you collect? Latency p50/p95, throughput, tokens/sec, GPU util, and kernel occupancy?

Alex: Yes. Also measured per-request tail latency under bursty arrivals (Poisson +/- 30%), and end-to-end cost estimate (tokens/sec normalized to A100 baseline). Perf-bot posted microbenchmarks for kernels too.

perf-bot: Kernel microbenchmarks: fused-attn-v2 on A100 showed 7% better median latency for seq<=512, but cold-start KV flush caused 12% p95 increase under streaming workloads. Fallback kernels have higher variance. (See attached csv in CI run 2026-03-10_176995).

Jin: You mentioned a regression after kernel-selector change — details?

Alex: After we flipped selector to prefer fused-attn-v2 for all devices when seq<1024, we saw p95 regressions for streaming small-turn workloads on T4/A10. Root cause: fused-attn-v2 ignores a small shared cache-path that our continuous-batcher relies on to quickly append KV frames, forcing extra CUDA memcopies. On A100/H100 the memcopies are masked by compute, but on T4/A10 they dominate.

Maria: Oof. So we need different per-GPU heuristics. Any quick wins?

Alex: Yes — I tested a token-aware queue policy that caps tokens-per-batch based on device memory-bandwidth estimate and expected KV-copy cost. Results: improved p95 on T4/A10 by ~18% vs fusion-only, with <3% loss on A100/H100 throughput.

Sam: Can you paste the recommended numeric settings you found? We need defaults for 1) max_batch_size and 2) max_tokens_per_batch and 3) queue policy per GPU type.

Alex: Recommended conservative defaults based on our mixed chat workload (seq p50=64, p95=256):

- T4: max_batch_size=12, max_tokens_per_batch=2048, queue_policy=token-aware (token_budget_target=0.65)
- A10: max_batch_size=16, max_tokens_per_batch=3072, queue_policy=token-aware (token_budget_target=0.7)
- L4: max_batch_size=20, max_tokens_per_batch=4096, queue_policy=token-aware (token_budget_target=0.7)
- A100: max_batch_size=32, max_tokens_per_batch=8192, queue_policy=priority-by-length (token_budget_target=0.9)
- H100: max_batch_size=48, max_tokens_per_batch=12288, queue_policy=priority-by-length (token_budget_target=0.92)

Note: token_budget_target is fraction of device token capacity we aim to fill before dispatch. Token-aware policy penalizes adding large-turn requests if it would push budget over target.

Jin: Those look aggressive for H100 but fine. How did KV cache behavior influence these numbers?

Alex: Two ways:
1) Prefix reuse reduces effective tokens-per-request; on A100/H100 that lets us push higher tokens_per_batch because compute masks copy overhead. On low-memory-bandwidth GPUs (T4/A10) KV-copy overhead increases with batch size -> pick lower tokens_per_batch.
2) When requests share prefixes, batching by length hurts (it groups long prefixes), so token-aware policy that prefers grouping short-turns first gave better end-to-end p95.

Maria: Any regression tests we should add to CI to avoid rolling fused-attn globally again?

Alex: Propose adding an integration perf test with representative streaming traces (short-turn heavy) on T4 and A10 in CI canary. Fail if p95 increases >8% vs baseline. Also add a kernel-selector gating check that simulates KV-append path and measures memcpy vs compute overlap.

perf-bot: CI job added: ci/perf/streaming_short_turns_t4 (run on schedule). Will post nightly diffs.

Sam: Did you try dynamic scaling where we relax max_batch_size when GPU util < threshold?

Alex: Yes — simple controller: if GPU_util<40% for 10s, increase max_batch_size by 25% (cap at device max). That reduced cold-period latency and increased throughput, but we observed oscillation for bursty traffic. Stabilized when adding hysteresis (apply change only if util sustained for 30s).

Jin: Action items?

Alex: 1) Roll back global fused-attn-v2 selector for T4/A10 and pin to fallback kernel until we implement KV-copy-aware fused kernel. 2) Update runtime defaults to the per-GPU numbers above. 3) Add CI perf tests and kernel gating check. 4) Add telemetry dims: tokens_per_dispatched_batch, queue_policy, token_budget_target to Console dashboards.

Maria: I'll open a PR to update defaults + document rationale. Sam/Jin can own CI tests + kernel gating.

Sam: I'll take CI perf tests.

Jin: I'll look at kernel gating and a patch to fused-attn to surface KV-append cost.

Alex: Thanks — I'll paste the raw perf CSVs to the PR and link the microbench outputs. Quick snippet of the perf-check command I used:
```
perf-runner --model open-13b-q --gpu A10 --workload streaming.json --max-batch 16 --max-tokens 3072 --policy token-aware --runs 200
```

Maria: :thumbsup: sounds good. Let's not forget to update release notes about the selector change and the temporary rollback.

perf-bot: Note: CI regression threshold set to p95 > +8% triggers rollback label.

Alex: I'll create the rollback RFC and tag @ops for scheduled rollout window. End of thread.
